And I don't aim to tell them.|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="The Pandora Effect">{{StoryCite|story=The Pandora Effect|book=The Empire Strikes Back Monthly 151}}</ref>}}
The word '''Ape''' described various [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of creatures related to [[Primate/Legends|primates]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in shape. The facial traits of the [[Sanyassan/Legends|Sanyassans]] were often described as being "ape-like"<ref name="ISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> or "simian".<ref name="dbSan">{{DB|species|marauder|Sanyassan Marauders}}</ref>

{{Species-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
In real life, the words "ape" and "monkey" cannot be used interchangeably; the former describes a class of large and tailless semi-sentient humanoid primates, while the latter refers to smaller creatures having a tail and cheek pouches, among other differences.<ref name="Apes and monkeys">{{WebCite|url=http://nationalzoo.si.edu/Animals/Primates/Facts/Primateness/Differences/default.cfm|text=Differences Among Prosimians, Monkeys, and Apes|archivedate=20051109102517}}</ref> In ''Star Wars'' literature, however, the two names have been used alternatively&mdash;the Sanyassans have been described as both "monkeylike"<ref name="GSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> and "ape-like".<ref name="ISWU" />
